chunks.text: To follow what they're forecasting, it helps to know the Sun has a rhythm.
Its face gets dark blotches called sunspots.
Each one is a place where the Sun's magnetism bursts up through the surface.
For a few years the spots grow more and more crowded.
Then they thin out, until the face is nearly bare again.
One full rise and fall takes about eleven years.
Scientists call it the solar cycle, and they number each round.
The round that's just beginning, in late twenty nineteen, is round twenty-five.
